title: Histopathological Classification of Canine Cutaneous Round Cell Tumors Using Deep Learning: A Multi-Center Study
summary: A multicenter CNN ensemble classified canine cutaneous round-cell tumor histotypes from histopathology images, using 117 cases across five histotypes and 45 mast-cell tumors. Evaluation was retrospective and image-level; it does not establish tumor-mechanism discovery or prospective veterinary benefit.
ai_technology: Deep convolutional networks classify canine cutaneous round-cell tumors from histopathology images.
organization: PoliToBIOMed Lab, Biolab, Department of Electronics and Telecommunications, Politecnico di Torino, Turin, Italy.

evidence.tested: multicenter canine cutaneous round-cell tumor dataset includes 117 cases across five histotypes plus 45 mast-cell tumors; patch-level CNN ensemble and image-level voting classify histotypes/grade. This is retrospective veterinary histopathology classification, no claim of new tumor biology.
evidence.unknown: The evaluation is retrospective and image-level; prospective clinical performance and external replication were not established.
evidence.ai_role: Deep convolutional networks classify canine cutaneous round-cell tumors from histopathology images.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
